newsitem.title: MEXICO: Aging Mexican labor leader hospitalized - reports.
newsitem.headline: Aging Mexican labor leader hospitalized - reports.

text.p: Ageing Mexican labour leader Fidel Velazquez was brought to a hospital on Thursday, television news programmes said.
The 97-year-old chief of the six-million member Mexican Workers Confederation was said to be tired and dehydrated.

Velazquez was being treated in a military hospital and was in a delicate condition, a report on 24 Horas said. His doctor, Salomon Jasqui, told news programme Hechos that the union leader was "feeling a little weak."
The ailing but still powerful union boss's unwavering support for nine presidents has made him a living symbol of Mexico's monolithic political system.
But he has been treated in hospitals for various health problems, most recently in April with an intestinal infection.
Progressively going deaf and blind, losing the use of one arm and needing help to walk, the cigar-chomping Velazquez has refused to contemplate resigning as union chief.
